description: b = a then a[i] = x is visible through b: alloc'd arrays are mutable buffers, unlike Elixir's immutable values. Options: forbid aliasing writable arrays, copy-on-write, or a uniqueness check (Perceus-style refcount == 1). Document the choice in README.

comments.text: Per 'Should a kernel body also run as plain Elixir?' (defk-dtw.6): Elixir mode is normative, so its result is the expected one. Decide to match Elixir here, or list the difference as a divergence.

Per 'What is the one rule a kernel author keeps in their head?' (defk-dtw.7): aliasing on write is a divergence and must be removed (copy on aliased write, or reject the aliasing at compile time). Arrays mean binaries, writes mean rebinding.
Per defk-dtw.16: until decided, aliasing cases go in the Defk.Divergences registry (defk-63k); done requires it empty.

Resolution: value semantics, as Elixir.
- Mechanism: static copy-on-write. At a write whose array has another live binding, copy, else write in place; no runtime refcount (Perceus-style rc kept unbuilt unless conservative copies hurt a target workload). Copy conservatively where uniqueness can't be proven. Swaps copy nothing. Rejected: a compile error (Elixir has no copy/1, and it rejects valid snapshots).
- Input arrays become writable: copied once before the first write, the caller's binary never mutated (defk-dtw.9 holds). This is how HLL update_many is written naturally.
- Write rule (the one place the subset defines rather than inherits meaning, since out[i] = v isn't Elixir syntax): an array write updates that variable from the write onward, through enclosing loops and branches; no other variable sees it. Rebinding a whole array inside a loop body and using it after the loop is a compile error. Scalar rebinding keeps Elixir scoping (probe: x = x + i in a for doesn't escape, as in Elixir).
- Inserted copies: no warning; listed in the fast-path report if adopted, and documented in docs/language.md.
- Glossary: Array added to CONTEXT.md.
Build: defk-auo (blocks the HLL workload).

title: Decide array value semantics (aliasing on write)
